reason: S1 adds an entire 7Zip parsing and decompression attack surface. H0 registers it indirectly through archive_read_support_format_all, so archive_read_format_7zip_bid can inspect inputs, but H0 has no 7Zip seed in files[] and only mutates less than 1% of existing ISO, CAB, LZH, TAR, ZIP, RAR, and other non-7Zip images. It therefore lacks adequate input semantics to reliably pass the six-byte 7Zip signature and structural/CRC requirements needed to exercise the new header, stream, folder, codec, and data-processing paths. This gap did not exist in S0 because ARCHIVE_FORMAT_7ZIP and the 7Zip reader were newly introduced by S1.
evidence: S1 adds the public entry point archive_read_support_format_7zip and the format identifier ARCHIVE_FORMAT_7ZIP.
S1 adds archive_read_support_format_7zip.c with 2,574 lines of new parsing, seeking, allocation, CRC, codec-selection, and decompression behavior.
archive_read_support_format_all now calls archive_read_support_format_7zip, and H0 calls archive_read_support_format_all before archive_read_open_memory.
slurp_central_directory additionally requires a valid 32-byte start header, matching CRCs, valid offsets, and parseable kHeader or kEncodedHeader structures before deep processing is reached.
H0 files[] contains no .7z archive or identified 7Zip image.
H0 begins with fixed non-7Zip reference archives and changes fewer than 1% of their bytes, which does not provide reliable control over valid 7Zip structure and encoded data.
recommended_action: Add at least one valid 7Zip reference archive to H0's files[] corpus, preferably covering ordinary and encoded headers plus supported codecs, so mutations preserve enough 7Zip structure to exercise archive_read_format_7zip_read_header, slurp_central_directory, read_StreamsInfo, and archive_read_format_7zip_read_data.
